newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung meets top China envoy.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung meets top China envoy.

text.p: Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa had his first formal contact with Beijing's envoy in the territory on Monday, barely a week after this former British colony returned to Chinese rule.
Veteran diplomat Ma Yuzhen paid a courtesy call to Tung's office in the Central business district and they shook hands for photographers before disappearing behind closed doors.
Neither side revealed the contents of this first formal dialogue, but one source said afterwards: "They discussed the work of the Foreign Ministry here in Hong Kong."
Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule and is now a special Chinese region with a high degree of autonomy.
Hong Kong runs all its own domestic affairs, but foreign affairs and defence are strictly in Beijing's hands.
Ma's office, the Office of the Commissioner, handles Hong Kong's external affairs and serves as a channel to Beijing.

His courtesy call follows a surprise move by Tung last week to set up official high-level links between Hong Kong and Taiwan, Beijing's arch-rival, sparking speculation as to whether Tung had sought approval from Beijing beforehand.

Later, though, in a move seen as bolstering Hong Kong's promised autonomy, a Foreign Ministry official in Beijing said that ties between Hong Kong and Taiwan were not a question of diplomacy (and therefore Beijing's sole responsibility), but an internal affair between two parts of China.
China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since the former Chinese Nationalist government lost the civil war to the communists in 1949 and took refuge on the island.
